description: 5 exemplars (one German) + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-10-14 under road-to-one-upstream-that-checks-what-leaves, whose step 1.2 corrected this skill's source_learning path and so brought it into check_routing_coverage's touched-skill scope. Exemplars cover the four intake shapes the skill's own 'When to use' names: a mistake that has recurred, a pattern worth reusing, the post-task reflection, and the rule-or-skill question itself — plus the audit-log pattern whose count already satisfies the repetition gate. Near-misses are three neighbours that all end in a written artefact and are somebody else's job: writing the skill once the kind is decided (skill-writing), recording an architectural choice (decision-record / ADR), and parking a durable cross-run lesson in memory (memory-consolidation). Counterexamples guard the word 'learning': a machine-learning feature question and a request for onboarding material both say learning and ask for no rule or skill.

queries.q: that's the third time this week we forgot to update the callers after a rename — make it stick
this review checklist worked really well, capture it so we reuse it next time
task is done — what did we learn here that's worth keeping?
should this become a rule or a skill? it's a constraint but it needs a procedure too
wir stolpern ständig über dasselbe Problem — mach daraus eine dauerhafte Regel
write the SKILL.md for the deploy-checklist skill we agreed on — frontmatter, triggers, procedure
queries.note: the kind is already decided; this is the authoring step → skill-writing

queries.q: we chose Postgres over DynamoDB for the event store — write that down so nobody reopens it
queries.note: a durable decision with alternatives and a revisit-if → decision-record / ADR

queries.q: remember for future sessions that our staging DB resets every Sunday night
queries.note: a durable fact for the memory layer, not guidance to encode → memory-consolidation

queries.q: would a learning-to-rank model improve our search results page?
put together a learning path for new backend hires — what should they read in week one?
queries.note: says learning, asks for onboarding material rather than a rule or skill
